articles.title: Microsoft AI Releases Microsoft-Decision-1: A Qwen3.5-9B Decision-Scoring Model
articles.summary: Microsoft released Microsoft-Decision-1, a decision-scoring model designed for routing, classification, verification, and agent control. The model returns calibrated probabilities for fixed answer options rather than generating text, is post-trained from Alibaba’s Qwen3.5-9B, and is available through Microsoft Foundry and OpenRouter.
articles.advisor_relevance: This points to continued enterprise AI platform evolution, with Microsoft adding specialized models that may improve reliability and control in agentic workflows. For advisors, the relevance is less about a single model release and more about the broader trend toward production-ready AI orchestration, verification, and decision automation within major cloud and AI platforms.

articles.title: Kingston University chosen to lead UK’s first waste and recycling robotics hub
articles.summary: Kingston University will lead the UK’s first dedicated waste and recycling robotics adoption hub, NORAH, as part of a £40 million government-backed robotics adoption scheme funded by Innovate UK. The £3.6 million project will test and validate robotic sorting systems on real contaminated waste streams to improve material recovery, reduce landfill, and support automation deployment in a sector where fewer than 5% of facilities currently use automation.
articles.companies: ["Kingston University", "Innovate UK", "University of Kent", "West London Waste Authority"]
articles.advisor_relevance: This is a concrete example of public-sector funding being used to move robotics from lab settings into difficult industrial environments. While no public robotics vendors are named, the project highlights potential second-derivative demand for computer vision, advanced sensing, robotic sorting cells, simulation, systems integration, and automation services tied to recycling and circular-economy infrastructure.

articles.title: UK’s National Composites Centre to lead business support for new £9.8 million Greater South West robotics hub
articles.summary: The UK’s National Composites Centre will lead one-to-one business advisory services for the new £9.8 million Greater South West Robotics Adoption Hub. The hub, led by Bristol Robotics Laboratory with University of Bristol, UWE Bristol and 23 partners, will help regional businesses assess automation opportunities, build investment cases and connect with robotics expertise, finance and demonstrations ahead of full operation by January 2027.

articles.title: Boston Dynamics gives more insight into its redesigned humanoid hand

The company emphasized modularity, durability, high-fidelity simulation, and sim-to-real reinforcement learning as key elements supporting faster testing and future deployment. Boston Dynamics is testing the hand on industrially relevant tasks such as tool use, cable handling, and manipulating screws.
articles.advisor_relevance: This article highlights continued progress in humanoid robotics from prototype capability toward manufacturable, durable systems designed for real-world industrial tasks.
